newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China lobby blasts Patten on toadying allegations.
newsitem.headline: China lobby blasts Patten on toadying allegations.

text.p: Members of the pro-China lobby in Hong Kong on Wednesday angrily accused British Governor Chris Patten of trying to split the local population by accusing them of inviting interference from Beijing.

Raymond Wu, a member of the influential China-controlled Preparatory Committee working on details of Hong Kong's handover to China next year, said the governor's accusations in an annual policy speech on Wednesday were "sheer nonsense".
"I wonder on what basis he can say something like that," Wu said. "He wants to divide Hong Kong people. He wants to give an impression someone is selling out the interest of Hong Kong."
Another leading pro-China politician, Tam Yiu-chung, said Patten was venting his own frustration after failing to get China to agree to his electoral reforms in Hong Kong.
"Obviously, he is trying to find a scapegoat to air his frustration because China has vowed to reverse his reforms after 1997," Tam told reporters.

Patten said earlier in his swansong annual policy speech that people in the colony who appealed to Beijing on various issues were inviting interference by China in Hong Kong policy matters, which he said would undermine autonomy after Britain hands back the territory at midnight next June 30.
Although Patten named no names, this was widely interpreted to be a criticism of pro-China business people.
"He should point out those who he is talking about," one of China's senior officials in Hong Kong, Zhang Junsheng, said after hearing the speech.
In a 1984 Sino-British treaty on the handover, China pledged to permit Hong Kong a high degree of autonomy in running its affairs and to maintain its capitalist way of life for 50 years.
But increasingly critics accuse Beijing of meddling both in Hong Kong's politics and in its commercial affairs.
